newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FULL TEXT-St George, Advance merger.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FULL TEXT-St George, Advance merger.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd and Advance Bank Ltd announced on Monday they had agreed to merge. A full text of their announcement follows.

The Boards of St George Bank Limited and Advance Bank Australia Limited today announced that they had signed an agreement to merge through a Scheme of Arrangement in a transaction valued at A$2.65 billion.
The merged company, St George Bank Limited, will be the largest regional bank in Australia, with over A$40 billion in assets, deposits of A$22 billion and shareholders' equity of A$3.5 billion.

Based on the 11 October 1996 closing price of $8.95 per ordinary share in St George Bank, the company's market capitalisation would be A$4.5 billion, placing St George Bank in the top 25 listed Australian companies.

In announcing the merger, the Chairman of St George Bank, Mr Frank Conroy said: "this creates a new force in Australian retail banking, one with a far greater capacity to compete with the four majortrading banks.

"It will combine the respective strengths of the two best banks in New South Wales and the best bank in South Australia to enhance service levels to customers and create significant value for shareholders."
Mr Jim Sweeney will be Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of the Bank.
TERMS OF THE TRANSACTION

St George Bank is offering A$7.30 for each Advance Bank share in a package of A$2.10 in cash, a special cash dividend of A$0.20 per share and new St George Bank shares up to a value of A$5.00 per Advance Bank share (up to a maximum 0.625 St George Bank shares for each Advance Bank share).
The consideration of A$7.30 per share, represents a 20 percent increase over the average Advance Bank share price over the last five trading days.
Advance Bank shareholders will also receive an Advance Bank interim dividend which is expected to be $0.20, payable in February 1997.

The number of St George Bank shares to be issued to Advance Bank shareholders will be based on the weighted average St.George Bank share price over a period of 20 business days prior to final shareholder approval of the merger.

Based on St George Bank's closing share price on 11 October 1996, of A$8.95 (adjusted to exclude St George Bank's January 1997 dividend) the transaction would have resulted in St George Bank issuing 209 million new shares to Advance Bank shareholders, or an exchange ratio of 0.575 St George Bank shares for each Advance Bank share.
However, the total number of St George Bank shares to be issued will be capped at a maximum of 227 million.

As part of the Merger Implementation Agreement, Advance Bank has agreed to reimburse St George Bank in certain circumstances for costs and losses, up to $100 million, if Advance Bank is acquired by a third party.
The merger is conditional upon a range of events, including shareholder approval, regulatory approvals and a reciprocal due diligence review over the next fifteen business days.
The merger is expected to be completed by April 1997.

Merger Financing to Include Capital Raising of up to $360 million. St George Bank will finance the merger through a combination of existing cash resources, new ordinary shares issued to Advance Bank shareholders and a new capital issue of up to A$360 million.
The capital issue will proceed upon completion of the acquisition of Advance Bank. Terms of the issue will be determined at that time.
Following the issue, St George Bank's proforma capital adequacy will be over 10 percent.

Tribute to Mr Jim Service; Mr John Thame to Join St.George Bank Board Mr Conroy paid tribute to the Chairman of Advance Bank, Mr Jim Service AM. Mr Conroy said, "Mr Service has announced that he will step down at the conclusion of this transaction.
He has been a magnificent contributor to the banking and finance industry over the last 37 years, having previously been the Chairman of the Civic Permanent Building Society.
He became a Board member of Advance in 1986 and Chairman in 1992 and has guided the bank to be a market leader, creating enormous shareholder value, over that time.
Mr Service has been a strong supporter of the regional bank sector and prominent in industry affairs. He holds strong views on the value of competition".

Mr Conroy also confirmed that Mr Service had been instrumental in bringing Advance and St.George to the point where each Board recognised it was in the best interests of shareholders to pursue a merger.

Mr Conroy said "I am delighted that Mr Thame has accepted our invitation to join the St.George Bank Board. Mr Thame brings with him over 25 years experience in the banking industry and his extensive experience and insights will be invaluable in integrating Advance Bank and St.George Bank".
SUBSTANTIAL MERGER COST SAVINGS; INTEGRATION TO BE MANAGED CAREFULLY

The merger will create the third largest bank in New South Wales and the largest bank in South Australia. The merged bank will be known as St George Bank and the St George brand name will be adopted throughout the entire Australian operations, with the exception of South Australia, where the BankSA brand will be retained. Upon completion, the merged entity will have 7,913 employees and 607 branches.

Management of the two banks has conducted a thorough review of the expense base of the combined institution and estimate that a net reduction is achievable of A$140 million before tax in annual expenses, or approximately 15 percent of the combined banks' expense base for the year ended 31 May, 1996.
Consequently, St George Bank anticipates that the transaction will increase its earnings per share before deducting goodwill amortisation.
The full merger cost savings are expected to be achieved within approximately 30 months.

Mr Sweeney said that it is inevitable that there will be redeployment of staff and some redundancies. However, these will take place over several years on a carefully managed basis to limit uncertainty.
As a general principle management and staff of the new bank will be selected on merit from both institutions.
External advisors will be appointed to assist with management selection and the integration process.
Further, a Board committee, including Mr John Thame, will oversee the integration process.

"St.George Batik will rely as much as possible on normal staff turnover to reduce staff numbers", Mr Sweeney said. "Branch rationalisation will proceed only following a careful review of the suitability of St.George Bank and Advance Bank branches in each area and the expected business activities of the merged bank.
"We expect that a mix of both St.George Bank and Advance Bank branches will be retained, Customer convenience will be a priority".

St George Bank expects to incur restructuring costs of $50 million in the 12 months following closing of the merger. These costs will be accounted for as an adjustment to goodwill incurred in relation to the transaction and will not impact the underlying earnings of the Bank.
ENHANCED COMPETITION

Mr Conroy emphasised the pro-competition benefits of the merger for existing and future customers. Ile stated that, with an enlarged distribution network, workforce and capital base, St George Bank would be exceptionally well positioned to be a market leader in offering competitive lending and deposit products.

St George Bank has considered the ACCC's new merger guidelines and is satisfied that the merger of St.George Bank and Advance Bank will not breach the guidelines, including the HHI threshold, in any Australian state.
"The importance to New South Wales and South Australia banking consumers of having a strong, independent regional bank cannot be overstated.
This merger cements St.George Bank and BankSA as the critical competitors in each of those markets" Mr Conroy said.
He said that the need to achieve lower costs was a critical factor in bringing the two banks together.
CS First Boston is the financial advisor to St George Bank in relation to the transaction.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
